q: What structural system did Egyptian architecture use?
n: Columns carrying stone beams.

q: Which style has battered walls, no windows and gorge cornices?
n: All three are Egyptian traits.

q: Which civilization built structures on platforms 6 to 10 meters high, with a conical shape and pipe holes?
n: Per the MST answer key: West Asiatic.

q: What type of column is characterized by a lotus or papyrus capital, commonly found in Egyptian architecture?
n: Per the MST answer key: Lotiform column.

q: What is the columned hall of an Egyptian temple, meant to suggest a papyrus marsh, called?
n: Hypostyle means under pillars.

q: Which Roman building still has the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome?
n: The Pantheon's dome is unreinforced concrete.

q: What is the largest surviving Roman triumphal arch, finished in AD 315?
n: It marks Constantine's victory at the Milvian Bridge.

q: Which was the largest Roman circus and one of the biggest arenas ever built?
n: It held roughly 150,000 spectators.

q: Who began the construction of the Great Hypostyle Hall in the Temple of Karnak?
n: Seti I began the hall; Ramesses II completed it.

q: What were Roman aqueducts for?
n: They carried water to cities.

q: How did the Egyptians make a level base for the pyramids?
o: By cutting trenches, filling them with water and marking the waterline
n: The water surface gave a datum.

q: What method was used to transfer 2-ton stones during the construction of the pyramids?
o: Lifted them one by one on top of the other
Used rolled logs to move and position them
n: Per the MST answer key: Used rolled logs to move and position them.

q: Who was chief architect of the Great Pyramid of Giza?
n: Hemiunu was Khufu's vizier.

q: What is the name of the ancient stone figure with the body of a lion and the head of a human?
n: A sphinx has a lion body and a human head.

q: Who designed the Step Pyramid of Zoser?
n: Imhotep, the first named architect.

q: Which architect was deified and honored during the reign of Rameses?
n: Per the MST answer key: Imhotep.

q: What is the pool in Egyptian temples used for ritual purification called?
n: Karnak has a large sacred lake.

q: What massive gateway fronted Egyptian temples, carved and often flanked by obelisks?
n: Twin tapering towers.

q: What tall, four-sided tapering monument symbolized the sun god Ra?
n: Its tip caught the first sunlight.

q: What was the prototype of the Egyptian pyramid?
n: Stacked mastabas formed the step pyramid.

q: In Roman work, opus tessellatum is:
n: Tesserae set in mortar.

q: Which Roman wall facing forms a net-like diagonal pattern?
n: Reticulum means net.

q: What was the warm room of a Roman bath?
n: Tepid means lukewarm.

q: What was the sweating room of a Roman bath?
n: Sudor means sweat.

q: What were the bedrooms of a Roman domus called?
n: Cubiculum, plural cubicula.

q: What is the triangular gable above the entablature?
n: The pediment closes the roof end.

q: Where is the pediment on a Doric temple?
n: It sits on the cornice at the gable ends.

q: What does the pediment of a Classical temple hold?
o: The tympanum, often filled with mythological sculpture
n: The tympanum carries the sculpture group.

q: What is a wide, low-pitched gable over a colonnade or a main section of a façade?
n: The tympanum is only its inner field.

q: In Greek temples, the cella is also called the:
n: The inner shrine holding the cult statue.

q: The Treasury of Atreus at Mycenae is also known as the:
n: A tholos (beehive) tomb.

q: Where did the agora originate?
n: The Greek public marketplace.

q: What was the long colonnaded hall of Greek cities?
n: Stoas lined the agora.

q: What open, colonnaded building, often very long, served as a public meeting place?
n: The stoa sheltered public life.

q: Who was the Roman architect and engineer of the 1st century BC?
n: Author of De Architectura.

q: What was the Colosseum mainly for?
n: Games and spectacles.

q: What is the effect of using a rib vault in architecture?
n: Rib vaults concentrate loads on piers, freeing walls for larger windows.

q: Which temple has a circular plan under a dome about 142 ft across, praised by Jefferson as a model of the spherical arch?
n: Jefferson modeled the Rotunda on it.

q: Which Egyptian temple at Thebes is known for its grand colonnades and obelisk?
n: Luxor Temple, linked to Karnak.

q: What stone was mainly used to build Luxor Temple?
n: Nubian sandstone from Gebel el-Silsila.

q: Luxor Temple wasn't built for a cult god's daily rites. It was dedicated to:
n: It celebrated the rejuvenation of royal power.

q: Whatconstruction system was employed in the construction of the Parthenon?
n: The Parthenon is trabeated (post and lintel).

q: Which order was used for the Parthenon's peristyle?
n: A Doric peristyle (with an Ionic frieze inside).

q: What is the name of Figure A?
n: Figure A is the Arch of Constantine beside the Colosseum.

q: What is the name of Figure B?
n: Figure B is the Parthenon.

q: What is the name of Figure C?
n: Figure C is the Pantheon.

q: What is the name of Figure D?
n: Figure D is the Circus Maximus.

q: What is the name of Figure E?
n: Figure E is the Erechtheion.
